answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identities to seismic pulse interferometry. Nodes prove uniqueness by timing acoustic reflections across a stone bridge, a walnut orchard, and a desert oasis. Simulating multiple agents forces an attacker to deploy discrete geophone stations at separate sites, incurring genuine hardware and property costs. However, ambient ground vibrations from passing traffic can distort waveforms and cause false rejections.
